title: NASA and ESA facilities avoid major damage from wildfires in Spain
summary: NASA and ESA ground stations in Spain avoided major damage from wildfires. The facilities are critical for space operations.

title: SpaceX conducts 13th Starship test flight
summary: SpaceX successfully conducted the 13th suborbital test flight of its Starship vehicle on July 24, addressing issues from the previous flight and deploying functioning satellites for the first time.

title: ULA deals with financial challenges caused by Vulcan grounding
summary: United Launch Alliance secured a loan from its corporate parents to address financial challenges stemming from the grounding of its Vulcan Centaur rocket. The company is navigating the impact of the rocket's delay on its operations.

title: LatConnect 60 Unveils Proprietary AI Capabilities Following Growing Indo-Pacific Defence Interest in SWIRSAT
summary: LatConnect 60 introduced proprietary AI capabilities for its satellite Earth observation systems, responding to increased defense interest in the Indo-Pacific region for its SWIRSAT technology.

title: Office of Space Commerce to move ahead on mission authorization
summary: The Commerce Department is advancing plans for a voluntary mission authorization system to regulate novel space activities not covered by other agencies. This initiative aims to fill regulatory gaps in emerging space operations.

title: Lightning strikes Long March 3B after liftoff, Kinetica-1 launches 5 satellites
summary: A Long March 3B rocket successfully delivered its payload to orbit despite being struck by lightning shortly after liftoff. Separately, the Kinetica-1 launch carried five satellites into space.
company: China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation (CASC)

title: EU delays release of Copernicus imagery over Gulf of Oman
summary: The European Union delayed the release of Copernicus Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 imagery for 24 hours after a U.S. request citing concerns over the Gulf of Oman. The decision highlights potential geopolitical sensitivities in satellite data dissemination.

title: Air Force takes over troubled military GPS receiver program
summary: The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center will now oversee the development, integration, and sustainment of military GPS receiver equipment. This move aims to address issues with the program accessing the military’s encrypted GPS signal.
company: Air Force Life Cycle Management Center

title: NASA programs feel effects of workforce reductions
summary: Over two dozen major NASA projects have been impacted by a 20% reduction in NASA's civil servant workforce over the past year. This workforce reduction is causing significant effects across various programs within the agency.

title: Poland commits $745 million to EU’s IRIS² constellation project
summary: Poland has committed $745 million to the EU's IRIS² multi-orbit satellite internet constellation project. The investment aims to support the development of the constellation alongside other EU member states.

title: What happened to space horror movies?
summary: Space horror movies have largely disappeared from theaters in recent years, with only a few exceptions. The genre was once popular but has since faded from mainstream cinema.

title: I'm not an astronaut, but I went to the International Space Station (sort of)
summary: A non-astronaut experienced a simulated visit to the International Space Station, highlighting its continued existence as a marvel of human achievement.

title: We talk with astronaut Michael Foale about the 1997 Space Station Mir crisis: 'He took all the blame of the collision on his shoulders'
summary: Astronaut Michael Foale discusses the 1997 Space Station Mir crisis, taking full responsibility for a collision while crediting the crew for saving the station. He reflects on the incident as a pivotal moment in space station history.

title: This Week In Space podcast: Episode 220 — First on Mars
summary: Episode 220 of the 'This Week In Space' podcast celebrates the 50th anniversary of Viking 1's Mars landing, featuring discussions with Dr. Pascal Lee and Dr. Penny Boston.

title: An off-the-shelf camera could help us find more black holes smashing together
summary: An off-the-shelf camera could enhance the detection of black hole mergers by improving LIGO's instrumentation without requiring new technology development. This innovation addresses a longstanding challenge in gravitational wave detection.

title: NASA astronaut, 2 cosmonauts returning to Earth on July 26: Watch it live
summary: NASA astronaut Chris Williams and two Russian cosmonauts are scheduled to return to Earth from the International Space Station on July 26. Their homecoming will be broadcast live.

title: SpaceX's Starship megarocket makes the 'softest splashdown' ever after launching next-gen Starlink satellites in Flight 13 test (video)
summary: SpaceX successfully launched its Starship megarocket on its 13th test flight, deploying next-gen Starlink satellites and achieving the 'softest splashdown' ever. The mission marked a significant milestone with a surprising successful conclusion.

title: ZWO Seestar S30 Pro smart telescope review
summary: The ZWO Seestar S30 Pro is a compact, automated smart telescope featuring a higher resolution upgrade. This review highlights its advanced capabilities and compact design.

title: We boldly chat with 'Star Trek: Strange New Worlds' showrunners about space dinosaurs and Lovecraftian horrors for season 4 (interview)
summary: The showrunners of 'Star Trek: Strange New Worlds' discuss incorporating space dinosaurs and Lovecraftian horrors into season 4. They express enthusiasm about exploring these themes in the series.

title: What lurks beneath the volcanoes of Jupiter's moon Io? NASA's Juno probe just took a peek
summary: NASA's Juno probe has provided new insights into the subsurface of Jupiter's moon Io by studying its volcanoes. These findings could significantly impact how scientists understand volcanic activity across the solar system, including Earth.

title: NASA Astronaut Chris Williams, Crewmates Return from Space Station
summary: NASA astronaut Chris Williams and two Roscosmos cosmonauts returned to Earth after an eight-month mission aboard the International Space Station. The crew landed safely in Kazakhstan after departing the station.

title: NASA’s ESCAPADE Snaps Family Portrait of Earth, Moon
summary: NASA's ESCAPADE spacecraft captured images of Earth and the Moon during its journey to Mars. The photos were taken from a distance of 363,250 miles from Earth and 115,600 miles from the Moon.

title: New Crew Members Welcomed to International Space Station
summary: Three new crew members—Anna Kikina and Pyotr Dubrov of Roscosmos, and Anil Menon of NASA—arrived at the International Space Station on July 14, 2026. They were welcomed aboard the station on July 18, 2026, after launching from the Baikonur Cosmodrome.

title: NASA Announces New Spacecraft Technology Demonstration Mission at Moon
summary: NASA has announced a new spacecraft technology demonstration mission at the Moon, partnering with industry to advance cislunar infrastructure for the Artemis program. The CAPSTONE 02 mission, awarded to Advanced Space, will test rendezvous, autonomous navigation, and communication capabilities.

title: NASA to Support Blue Origin New Glenn Rocket Testing, Advance Artemis
summary: NASA and Blue Origin agreed to conduct second stage hot fire testing for New Glenn rocket at Stennis Space Center. The testing is part of a reimbursable Space Act Agreement to advance Artemis.

title: Hubble Spies One-Sided Spiral
summary: Hubble Space Telescope captured an image of spiral galaxy NGC 4654, which is located 72 million light-years away in the constellation Virgo. The galaxy's asymmetric structure is highlighted in the observation.

title: A Million-Panel Project
summary: Utah has inaugurated a massive solar power and battery storage facility, featuring a million panels. This project is one of the largest renewable energy initiatives in the region.

title: Curiosity Blog, Sols 4954–4960: Celebrating Our Rover Engineers Past and Present
summary: The Curiosity rover team celebrates the engineers who have worked on the mission, highlighting the contributions of the APXS instrument team. The blog post reflects on the ongoing operations and scientific achievements of the rover.

title: Look for NASA+ Now Streaming on Amazon Fire TV
summary: NASA+ is now available on Amazon Fire TV Channels, expanding access to its programming via Alexa-enabled devices. Future content may include science missions and test flights.

title: Crews Move Artemis IV Liquid Hydrogen Tank
summary: NASA crews transported the 130-foot-tall liquid hydrogen tank for Artemis IV from a production cell to a test building at the Michoud Assembly Facility in New Orleans on May 15, 2026. The tank will be part of the core stage for the Artemis IV mission.

title: Blue Origin to conduct New Glenn second stage hot fires on Stennis B-2 stand
summary: NASA and Blue Origin have finalized plans to hot-fire test the second stage of the New Glenn rocket at the Stennis B-2 stand. This marks a significant step in preparing the New Glenn rocket for its upcoming missions.

title: Starship Flight 13 achieves new firsts for SpaceX
summary: Starship Flight 13, featuring Booster 20 and Ship 40, achieved new milestones for SpaceX on its third attempt. This marks another step forward in SpaceX's development of the Starship system.

title: Soyuz MS-29 crew arrives at ISS, U.S. EVA completes Canadarm2 repairs
summary: The Soyuz MS-29 crew successfully arrived at the International Space Station (ISS), expanding the station's crew by three members. A U.S. extravehicular activity (EVA) completed repairs on the Canadarm2 robotic arm.

title: Path to Starship Flight 13 requires additional Booster 20 test
summary: SpaceX is preparing for Starship Flight 13, targeting July 23, but requires additional testing of Booster 20. The delay highlights ongoing challenges in the development of the Starship program.

title: Falcon 9 to launch MRV-1 robotic servicing spacecraft for Northrop Grumman
summary: SpaceX's Falcon 9 is scheduled to launch the Mission Robotic Vehicle (MRV-1) for Northrop Grumman from Florida. The MRV-1 is a robotic servicing spacecraft designed to perform in-space operations.

title: Launch Preview: Falcon 9, Starship, and Chinese rockets scheduled to launch
summary: SpaceX is preparing for a new launch attempt of Starship Flight 13 after a previous abort. Additionally, Falcon 9 and Chinese rockets are also scheduled for launches.

title: Making Progress: Relativity’s Terran R, Rocket Lab’s Neutron, and PLD Space’s Miura 5
summary: Three companies—Relativity Space, Rocket Lab, and PLD Space—are making progress on their respective launch vehicles: Terran R, Neutron, and Miura 5. While SpaceX's Starship has dominated recent headlines, these competitors are advancing their own reusable rocket programs.

title: China’s first recovered booster returns to port as LandSpace aims for first land recovery
summary: China achieved a milestone with the recovery of its first booster, and LandSpace is now aiming for the first land recovery of a booster.

title: Soyuz MS-29 launches new crew to ISS from Baikonur
summary: Soyuz MS-29 successfully launched a new crew to the International Space Station (ISS) from the Baikonur Cosmodrome. This marks another mission to maintain the orbital laboratory's operations.

title: Launch Preview: Soyuz to launch crew to ISS, Starship to fly another test flight
summary: Soyuz is set to launch a crew to the International Space Station (ISS), while SpaceX's Starship is scheduled for another test flight. Seven launches are planned globally this week.

title: ESA Delivers: 50 years booklet
summary: The European Space Agency (ESA) released a booklet highlighting 50 major achievements over its 50-year history. This commemorative publication celebrates the agency's significant milestones and contributions to space exploration.

title: The silicon brains steering next-generation antennas
summary: Next-generation antennas are being steered by advanced silicon-based systems, marking a significant technological advancement in space communications. This innovation is expected to enhance the performance and efficiency of satellite and space mission operations.

title: Plato's electronics ready for space
summary: ESA's PLATO spacecraft has completed key electromagnetic compatibility tests in the Maxwell Test Chamber, confirming its electronics are space-ready. The mission is now cleared for launch on an Ariane 6 rocket in March 2027.

title: Test firing at brand new green chemical propulsion lab
summary: A new green chemical propulsion lab conducted its first test firing. This marks a significant step in developing environmentally friendly propulsion technologies for space missions.

title: Upcoming ESA–Industry events on CM25 implementation
summary: ESA is hosting events to present the follow-up to CM25, inviting industry to discuss planned activities and opportunities. The events aim to facilitate direct exchange on implementation across ESA programmes.

title: One robotic arm to rule them all
summary: The article discusses a new robotic arm designed for space applications, highlighting its versatility and potential to standardize robotic operations in the space industry. This innovation could significantly enhance automation and reduce costs for future missions.

title: We’re back: Proba-3 ready for more science
summary: The Proba-3 mission's Coronagraph spacecraft and its ASPIICS instrument are fully operational and ready to resume formation flying to create artificial eclipses for scientific observations.

title: ESA’s Prodex programme brings scientific research to space
summary: ESA's Prodex programme has enabled the successful launch of the 4DSpace-Daedalus mission in Norway. The programme supports research institutes in participating in European space science activities and missions.

title: ESA Puts €65M Behind Europe’s First Lunar Ice Rover
summary: ESA has committed €65 million to Europe's first lunar polar ice exploration rover mission, led by ispace-Europe. This marks a significant step in Europe's lunar exploration efforts.

title: Lunar Outpost Plans to Fly NVIDIA Chips to the Moon
summary: Lunar Outpost is planning to send NVIDIA chips to the Moon, merging the semiconductor and lunar exploration industries. This move highlights the growing intersection of technology and space missions.

title: A Deep Dive into the Bluetooth Satellite Connectivity Market Following the FCC’s Proposal
summary: The FCC is proposing to open unlicensed Bluetooth and Wi-Fi frequencies for space-based communications. This move could significantly impact the Bluetooth satellite connectivity market.

title: FCC Filings Show Eutelsat is Working on a New 528-sat Constellation Beyond OneWeb
summary: FCC filings indicate Eutelsat is developing a new constellation of 528 satellites, separate from its OneWeb program. The company's comments suggest the 'Next' program is still in development.

title: NASA Puts $2B Price Tag on Nuclear Mars Mission
summary: NASA has announced a $2 billion price tag for the Space Reactor-1 Freedom, a fission-powered spacecraft intended for Mars missions. This marks the first interplanetary spacecraft powered by nuclear fission.

title: Intel Authorization Act Proposes Limiting Commercial EO Access
summary: The Intel Authorization Act aims to restrict commercial Earth observation (EO) satellite operators from sharing certain data with the public, framing EO data as a privilege rather than a right. This proposed legislation seeks to increase government control over commercially gathered EO information.

title: The UK Scraps the Department in Charge of UKSA
summary: The UK has decided to abolish the department overseeing the UK Space Agency (UKSA) during the Farnborough Air Show. This move comes as the new Prime Minister Andy Burnham seeks to reorganize government structures.

title: The UK and Space Florida Launch Joint Fund
summary: The UK and Space Florida have launched a joint fund to support projects with partners from both regions. This initiative aims to foster collaboration between the UK and Florida in space-related ventures.

title: Breaking Down the $686B Space Economy
summary: The global space economy reached a record $686 billion in 2025, according to the Space Foundation. This marks a significant growth in the industry's economic impact.

title: FCC Eyes Wi-Fi and Bluetooth Bands for Satellites
summary: The FCC is considering a proposal to permit unlicensed wireless devices like Wi-Fi and Bluetooth to communicate directly with satellites. This move aims to expand satellite connectivity options for consumer devices.

title: NASA to Support New Glenn Hot Fire Testing at Stennis Space Center
summary: NASA and Blue Origin will conduct second stage hot fire testing for the New Glenn rocket at NASA’s Stennis Space Center in Mississippi. This collaboration aims to advance the development of the New Glenn rocket.

title: Two Galileo Satellites Enter Service for Europe
summary: Two new Galileo satellites, SAT 33 and SAT 34, have entered service, enhancing Europe's satellite navigation system. The European Space Agency (ESA) announced their operational status, boosting capability and resilience.

title: Telco CEOs Shut Down the Idea of Satellite MVNO, Say LEO Isn’t a Threat to Broadband
summary: Telco CEOs rejected the idea of forming a satellite MVNO partnership, stating they do not view LEO satellite broadband as a significant competitive threat to traditional broadband services.

title: Space Is Coming for Silicon
summary: SpaceX has introduced Starmind, an AI satellite megaconstellation, marking a significant step in orbital data centers. Elon Musk highlighted the project as part of SpaceX's expanding space-based infrastructure.

title: Iceye and KT SAT Partner on Flood Intelligence in South Korea
summary: Iceye and KT SAT have partnered to provide flood monitoring solutions in South Korea for government and commercial entities. This is the first deployment of Iceye Solutions in the region.

title: Intellian Releases New Terminal for Iridium GMDSS Service
summary: Intellian has launched a new terminal for Iridium's GMDSS maritime safety service, utilizing the Iridium Certus 100 service. The terminal was announced on Thursday and is designed for use with the Global Maritime Distress and Safety System.

title: Frequency Electronics Reports Increased Demand From Proliferated Satellite Programs
summary: Frequency Electronics reported $18 million in recent contract wins, including an $11 million award from an undisclosed major aerospace prime contractor for a proliferated satellite program.

title: FCC Approves a New C-Band Auction
summary: The FCC has approved a new C-band auction where satellite operators will clear 160 megahertz of the upper C-band spectrum. This auction builds on previous efforts to reallocate C-band frequencies for wireless services.

title: Lite Coms Wins $22M Contract to Support Operational Readiness
summary: Lite Coms secured a $22 million contract from an unnamed government and defense customer to provide satellite communications for operational readiness. The company specializes in integration and manufacturing of satellite communication solutions.

title: FCC Overhauls Satellite Licensing, Adopts ‘Assembly Line’ Approach
summary: The FCC approved a major overhaul of its satellite and earth station licensing process, introducing a streamlined 'licensing assembly line' approach. This change aims to simplify and expedite the approval process for space-related licenses.
